key_insight: ScholarCatalyst introduces a benchmark for measuring whether AI can retrieve prior papers that genuinely inspire new research, not just papers that are topically similar. It captures the human skill of finding the right earlier idea that helps solve a new problem.
problem_solved: Current search and retrieval systems are good at finding relevant papers, but they struggle to identify the specific prior work that actually sparks or enables a research advance. This paper addresses the lack of a benchmark for evaluating that higher-level, inspiration-oriented retrieval ability.
method: Built a benchmark called ScholarCatalyst using papers as evidence of which prior works influenced completed research projects.
Collected author annotations through an automated pipeline to make large-scale labeling practical and scalable.
Frames retrieval as finding papers that inspired new research, rather than simply matching keywords or citations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a more realistic test of research-assistant systems, literature search tools, and scholarly recommendation models. It can help build systems that support discovery, ideation, and scientific progress, not just document retrieval.

paper_title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
